status_summary: No bill or Treasury statement to move the Coast Guard or ATF to Treasury, and no congressional examination of the idea, was found. The Justice Department's FY2026 request proposed folding ATF into the Drug Enforcement Administration, a move within Justice rather than to Treasury, but it was not carried out: a House subcommittee bill advanced 2025-07-15 would bar funds for shifting ATF functions, according to a news report, and the enacted appropriations law (Public Law 119-74, signed 2026-01-23) funds ATF at 1,585.0 million dollars as a separate bureau, per CRS. A Senate bill on Coast Guard leadership (S. 1190) keeps the Coast Guard in Homeland Security.

timeline.event: House Appropriations CJS subcommittee advanced the FY2026 bill that, per a news report, bars funds to move ATF responsibilities to other agencies and blocks the proposed ATF and DEA merger.
Public Law 119-74 (FY2026 Commerce, Justice, Science appropriations) is signed, funding ATF at 1,585.0 million dollars as a separate bureau, 40 million below FY2025, per CRS.

title: Examine returning the Coast Guard and ATF to Treasury
uncertainties: No bill, order or law moving the Coast Guard or ATF to Treasury was found. The Justice Department's FY2026 request to fold ATF into DEA, read through news summaries, was a move within Justice and was not carried out; the enacted text of Public Law 119-74 was not read, so a funding bar is unconfirmed. DHS pages are blocked and the defense authorization law was not read for Coast Guard provisions. The Unified Agenda rule lists on reginfo.gov for Treasury, Homeland Security and Justice (headed 'Agency Rule List - 2026') list no transfer; a transfer needs legislation, so the agenda is a weak test. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
